We don't absolutely need parties, but we have an electoral system that (stupidly and needlessly) rewards them. Meaning if the dems nominate Hillary, but Trump, Cruz, Kasich, Rubio, etc. run as independents, then Hillary wins every district -- typically with about 30% of the vote, but that's good enough if the other 70% is split.

First replace the voting system. Look for the ones that meet the cloneproof criteria.

Second remove any special privileges for (major) parties, such as the ones related to ballot access, guaranteed seats on "bipartisan" committees, access to public funds, etc.

Then political parties will still exist, but will be viewed by voters and candidates as optional.

I posted my opinion on electoral reform here.

Would like to hear your version.

Direct democracy on issues would fail, the general population can never be informed equally on all things. Individuals being elected to seats of power would also fail to be informed sufficiently on an equal breadth of issues. Even with political parties, there are attractors to certain issues, and other issues are ignored, and their are repellents to certain issues, which should be served, but the party is biased against them, or state interests in general (vs the electorates interests) is biased against them. You could argue parties fail here, but i think things would be worse without them, and single issue voting locally and nationally would create a more dysfunctional government.

Political parties are a necessary evil. They allow a broader range of issues to be served and governed over, and people can vote for their bias on the issues they represent. Again, less of the electorates issues they care for, would be served by voting unaligned individuals into power, rather than parties.

Parties are the natural outgrowth of our voting system. We only "need" them to organize ourselves for a win. What we're seeing in 2016 is the dems using their party structure to fight reform while the GOP has failed so far. If they run a 3rd party, the GOP mandarins will essentially have formed a new coalition with Hillary.

The reason I like Trump is because he's not a politician nor a Republican Party insider. He is a populist supported by the people, not the party. I could say the same for Bernie Sanders but I don't favor him because he dips too far into socialism.
